title: Taranga 15. The Lives of Sri Shyamananda and Others
html:
Shyamananda's letter to Srinivasa; Shyamananda in Utkala; Rasikananda (Rasika Murari): birth, dream, meeting and initiation; sankirtana at Dharenda, the conversion of the pashandas; the service of Govinda at Gopivallabhapura; the deeds of Rasikananda; the branches of Srinivasa and Narottama

1Glory to Gaura, Nityananda, Advaita, Gadadhara!
Glory, glory to Srivasa, Murari, Vakreshvara!

2Glory to Sri Mukunda, Gauridasa, Gadadhara!1
Glory to Pundarika Vidyanidhi, to Shuklambara!

3Glory to Suryadasa, Krishnadasa, Dhananjaya!
Glory to Narahari, Raghunandana, Vijaya!

4Glory to Vasu Ramananda, the abode of virtues!
Glory to Jagadisha and Sri Shankara, full of bliss!2

5Glory to Kashi Mishra, Kashishvara, Karnapura!
Glory, glory to Chakravarti Srinatha Thakura!

6Glory to Sri Sundarananda, to the lame Bhagavan!
Glory to Abhirama, the lord of Malini's life!

7Glory to Raghunatha Bhatta, Sanatana, Rupa!
Glory to Sri Bhugarbha and to Lokanatha, the king of bhakti!

8Glory to Sri Gopala Bhatta, to Raghunatha Dasa!
Glory, glory to Sri Jiva, renowned in the world!

9Glory to Krishnadasa Kaviraja, full of prema!
Glory to Vrindavana Dasa, the Vyasa of Gaura's lila!

10Glory to Haridasa, ever intoxicated with prema for the Name!
Glory to the ocean of mercy, Sri Acharya Srinivasa!

11Glory, glory to Narottama, glory to Ramachandra!
Glory, glory to Shyamananda, the giver of the jewel of bhakti!

12Glory, glory to the listeners, the abode of virtues!
Now listen with kind hearts to what I shall tell.

13One day Sri Acharya, to his own companions,3
greatly delighted, tells of Shyamananda's deeds.

14At that time two disciples of Sri Shyamananda
came with a letter to the Acharya's home.

15They gave Sri Shyamananda's letter to the Acharya;
reading the letter, the Acharya rejoiced in his heart.

16He showed great affection to Sri Shyamananda's disciples;
writing a letter with his news, he soon sent [them back].

17Reading the letter, Shyamananda was overwhelmed with joy.
Beautiful and spotless is the life of Sri Shyamananda.

18Earlier I briefly told what Shyamananda's way was;
now I shall tell a little of how he delivered living beings.

19Earlier, having come from Vraja to Sri Gauda-mandala,
he went by way of Ambika and swiftly set out for Utkala.

20Having made prema-bhakti manifest in his birthplace, the village of Dandeshvara-Dharenda, he goes on to Rayani.

21In Mallabhumi there is a village named Rayani;
beside the village is a river named the Suvarnarekha.4

22There the Suvarnarekha flows northward;
it destroys the great sins of all living beings.

23Near Rayani is a village named Barayita;
nearby is a lovely spot on the bank of the Dolanga river.5

24In Barayita Rama, the son of Dasharatha,
installed Shiva named Rameshvara.

25Ramachandra, with Janaki and Lakshmana, happily
stayed [there] some days, delighting in wandering through the forest.

26The ruler of that land is named Achyuta;
he delights in caring for his subjects, and his ways are very pure.

27In the village of Rayani the son of Achyuta is renowned;
he has two names, Sri Rasikananda and Sri Murari.

28Among the people he is known by the name Rasika Murari;
from a young age he has been learned in all the shastras.

29He is supremely diligent in serving his mother and father;
his mother, named Bhavani, is a wife wholly devoted to her husband.

30Murari's wife is Ichchha, endowed with virtues.
For some time [he] lived in the village of Ghantashila.6

31Ghantashila is on the bank of the Suvarnarekha;
there the Pandavas rested during their life in the forest.

32One day Murari, sitting there in solitude,
ponders in his heart where he will become a disciple.

33A voice came from the sky: "Do not worry:
here you will become a disciple of Sri Shyamananda."

34Hearing this, Rasika Murari rejoiced
and began to chant the mantra of Shyamananda's name.

35Moment by moment his longing grows beyond measure;
at the name of Prabhu Shyamananda streams [of tears] flow from his eyes.

36Murari passed almost the whole night in agitation;
at the close of the night a little sleep overcame him.

37In a dream Murari sees Shyamananda-deva:
supremely wonderful is the beauty of every limb of his body.

38Smiling, Sri Shyamananda says to Murari:
"When the night is over, at dawn you will find me here."

39Saying this, Shyamananda vanished from sight;
great bliss arose in Rasikananda's heart.

40The most wise Sri Rasika, at daybreak,
saying nothing to anyone, watches the road.

41Not far off Shyamananda comes joyfully,
with his disciples, Sri Kishoradasa and others, all around him.

42His body, full of beauty, shines like the sun;
his face is smiling, his broad chest captivates the heart.

43Taking the names of Sri Krishna Chaitanya and Nityananda,
he walks, overwhelmed with prema, swaying, swaying.

44Rasika Murari, seeing Prabhu Shyamananda,
fell to the ground in great bliss, touching his feet.

45Shyamananda, with joy in his heart, embraced him
and drenched Rasika with the tears of his own eyes.

46Sri Rasikananda considers himself blessed;
he gave his eyes over to the beauty of his own master.

47Shyamananda showed mercy to Murari:
in great joy he gave him initiation into the mantra of Radha and Krishna.

48With a joyful heart, having made Sri Rasikananda his disciple,
he entrusted him to the feet of Nityananda and Chaitanya.

49Rasika Murari was overwhelmed with prema;
tears ceaselessly stream from his eyes.

50He brought his own master to the village of Rayani
and was immersed in the ocean of the happiness of sankirtana.

51Such is Sri Rasika Murari's devotion to his guru —
how could I have the power to tell it with one mouth?

52Shyamananda tested Murari;
seeing Murari's conduct, he was filled with great joy.

53Shyamananda, staying there for some time,
made bhakti manifest and made many disciples.

54Shyamananda departs from Rayani,
surrounded on all sides by his dearest [companions].

55There was a certain practitioner of yoga named Damodara;
showing him mercy, he immersed him in bhakti-rasa.

56Having become a disciple of Sri Shyamananda, Damodara
ceaselessly weeps, saying, "Nitai, Chaitanya!"

57Seeing that rapture of prema, who could keep his composure?
Crying, "Bhakti is above all!", he dances.7

58Shyamananda-deva, having delivered Damodara,
wanders everywhere, distributing the jewel of bhakti.

59The prema-bhakti that merciful Shyamananda
made manifest in Balarampura cannot be told.

60Together with Kishora, Murari, Damodara and others8
he held a great, great festival in the village of Dharenda.

61Seeing Shyamananda, many people of the village,
overwhelmed with joy, forget great sorrow and grief.

62Shyamananda made disciples in place after place;
who would not be purified [even] by their names?

63Radhananda, Sri Purushottama, Manohara,
Chintamani, Balabhadra, Sri Jagadishvara,

64Uddhava, Akrura, Madhuvana, Sri Govinda,9
Jagannatha, Gadadhara, Sri Anandananda —

65with his disciples, Sri Radhamohana and others,
he always floats on the waves of the happiness of sankirtana.

66The great and wondrous pastimes of Sri Shyamananda
the poets describe, to the delight of all.

67Thus [it is said] in a song (raga Velavali):
Glory, glory to Shyamananda, full of joy!
Ceaselessly immersed in the rasa of prema for Gaura,
his body glistens with fresh thrills of bliss.

68He laments over the many deeds of Shyama and Gaura;10
the sweet beauty of his face steals one's very life.
Hearing of the virtues of the incomparable Lord's associates,
his lovely lotus eyes stream, stream [with tears].

69His heart overflows unceasingly; with thick drops of sweat
his bright tilaka trickles down.
A wondrous dance in the sweetest kirtana;
on his chest the tulasi garland gently sways.

70Most sweet is the singing; he sways [his head] in approval;
his arms curve gracefully, his hands are restless and lovely.
With the soles of his feet he keeps the tala in so many ways —
ah, ah! — Ghanashyama Dasa offers himself [for this].11

71In the village of Dharenda, Shyamananda with his companions
one day became greatly intoxicated in sankirtana.

72Mridangas and karatalas sound charmingly;
Sri Kishora and the other associates sing songs.

73From the very start, singing the qualities of Gaura and Nityananda,
the Vaishnavas became intoxicated and cannot keep their composure.

74From everyone's eyes streams of tears flow ceaselessly;
all roll on the ground, grey with dust.

75Thakura Shyamananda dances in the sankirtana;
the demigods rejoice to see those movements.

76The pashanda asuras, seeing that dance,
are overwhelmed with prema and weep, rolling on the ground.

77"Prabhu Shyamananda, deliver [us] this time!" —
saying this, they fall at [his] feet again and again.

78Looking at them all with a merciful glance, Shyamananda
plunged [them] into the ocean of the rasa of prema-bhakti.

79Thousands upon thousands of people come running, vying with one another;
there is nothing to compare with the joy of sankirtana.

80Before Shyamananda's qualities no one can keep composure;
such festive play he revealed in Sri Nrisimhapura.

81In Sri Gopivallabhapura he poured down a rain of prema;
the service of Sri Govinda he entrusted to Sri Rasika.12

82The great power of Rasikananda became known everywhere;
in his mercy he delivered robbers and pashandas.

83In his mercy he gave the jewel of bhakti to the yavanas;
from village to village he wandered with his disciples.

84The elephant that a wicked man set upon him — he made it a disciple
and engaged it in the service of Krishna and the Vaishnavas.13

85That wicked yavana king bowed down [before him];
heedless of home, how many beings he delivered!14

86Sri Rasikananda is ever intoxicated with sankirtana;
who is not overwhelmed by the songs of his qualities?

87Thus [it is said] in a song (raga Velavali):
Glory, glory to Rasika, Murari the true rasika!
Compassionate, destroyer of the stains of Kali,
whose pure qualities steal people's hearts. (Refrain.)

88Of mighty power, worthy of worship, most wondrous,
revealer of bhakti, giver of happiness, most steadfast.
Brimming with prema, bright like gold,
his exceedingly graceful body shines.

89His heart meditates on Shyamananda's feet;
every moment he drinks the rasa of sankirtana.
All his rasa is Gaurachandra; apart from Him — what shall I say? —
even in dreams he knows no other.

90His wondrous fame shines in the three worlds;
in the poems of the best poets it is known as peerless.
His life is wholly magnanimous and beautiful; even a little of it
the fallen Ghanashyama cannot understand.

91There is no end to the deeds of Sri Rasikananda;
he is ever overwhelmed by the qualities of Prabhu Shyamananda.

92Who is not charmed by the qualities of Sri Shyamananda?
In various ways [poets] sing of his life.

93Thus [it is said] in a song (raga Kamoda):
O friend of my life, Shyamananda, ocean of happiness,
ever overwhelmed by Gora's qualities!
Leaving home far behind, joyfully, to Ambikapura
he came, to the house of [his] Prabhu.15

94Seeing Hridaya Chaitanya, his eyes pour ceaseless tears,
and he falls to the ground, rolling.
Placing those feet on his head, surrendering himself,
he remains standing to one side.

95Seeing Shyamananda's ways, the Thakura, with affection,
kept him near and made him a disciple.
Showing great favour, teaching him the ways of bhakti,
he entrusted him to Nitai and Chaitanya.16

96After some days, as [he] was being sent to Vrajapura,
Shyamananda grew agitated.
Prabhu Nitai and Chaitanya blessed Shyamananda:
at his departure They gave [him] a garland as a sign of permission.

97Shyamananda walks along the road, floating in tears,
remembering the qualities of [his] Prabhu.
Alone, after some days he entered the land of Vraja,
having wandered through many tirthas.

98Seeing Sri Vrindaranya, he considers himself blessed;
in bliss he cannot stay steady.
Drenched with tears, he rolls on the ground;
his body is full of abundant thrills of joy.

99Going to Giri-Govardhana, he did what was in his heart;
coming to the bank of Sri Radha-kunda,
he was overwhelmed with prema; seeing [him], favour was shown him
by Sri Dasa Gosani, a treasury of virtues.

100He went to Sri Jiva and told him who he was;
he showed him mercy with fatherly affection.
Whatever desire [he] had was, as it were, fulfilled
through the mercy of Hridaya Chaitanya.

101He wandered the twelve forests, studied the books,
and became very skilled in service.
By way of Sri Gauda and Ambika he went and settled in Utkala
by the order of the Gosvamis.

102The pashanda asuras he intoxicated with Gora's qualities —
to whom did he not give bhakti?
The lowly float in bliss by a particle of Shyamananda's mercy —
who did not attain deliverance?

103Who will know his true nature? He is ever intoxicated with sankirtana;
his glory is known on earth.
With his own associates he delights in supreme joy;
in Utkala there is no limit to happiness.

104Whoever sees him even once cannot keep his composure —
how charming is that form!
Narahari says: will Rasikananda's Prabhu
ever come before these eyes?

105Again, raga Suhai:
Glory! The qualities of Sri Duhkhini Krishnadasa —
who has the power to tell them?
At the lotus feet of Hridaya Chaitanya ever
[abides] the bee of his mind.17

106He who in Vrindavana, in a fresh grove,
found Rai's anklet —
there the name Shyamananda became known; his
fine life — who will understand it?18

107Those in Utkala of utterly dull mind
who had not a trace of bhakti —
all of them he set afloat in the rasa of Gaura-prema
and made [that] land fruitful.

108My Shyamananda sorrows at others' sorrow,
Rasikananda's Prabhu.
What can I say of the mercy of him who never
abandons the lowly Narahari?

109This life of Shyamananda I have told in brief;
because of the book's length I could not describe it in detail.

110Shyamananda blessed Utkala and other lands;
hearing [of it], everyone in Gauda rejoiced.

111In Gauda the dear ones of Srinivasa and Narottama
are supremely skilled in bestowing the jewel of bhakti.

112[All this] spread ever on through the branches and sub-branches of both;
I shall tell a little — that which, when heard, soothes the heart.

113The dearest disciple of Srinivasa Acharya
is Ramachandra Kaviraja, peerless in qualities.

114Sri Ramachandra's disciple is Harirama Acharya;
all his extraordinary deeds are known everywhere.19

115Distributing the prema-bhakti of Sri Krishna Chaitanya,
he joyfully destroys the sins of living beings.

116In sankirtana he is ever supremely overwhelmed;
poets sing of that charming life.

117Thus [it is said] in a song (raga Pauravi):
Glory, glory to Sri Harirama, the best of acharyas,
whose wondrous life steals the heart!
His qualities are bright; he crushes calamity and pride;
his sweet form increases joy.

118He conquers the invincible asuras averse to the Lord's feet;
his fame is proclaimed in the world.
Supremely steadfast, he steals the composure of the steady;
compassionate of mind, he is exceedingly generous.

119Every moment he is mad with the fullness of Gaura-prema;
his gait is powerful, putting to shame a maddened king of elephants.
Greedy for the rasa of sankirtana, skilled in serving the Vaishnavas —
who can tell the limit of [his] happiness?

120His exposition of the Srimad-Bhagavatam and other books
is a peerless stream of nectar, full of rasa.
Sri Sri Krishna-raya is his life; what shall Narahari say?
[His] glory is boundless.20

121Sri Narottama's disciple is Ramakrishna Acharya,
a supreme pandita, a great arya on the path of bhakti.21

122He is very loving to the poor, the lowly and the destitute;
he destroys the doctrines of the pashandas — this is known everywhere.22

123He constantly relishes the rasa of sankirtana;
who does not sing of that charming life?

124Thus [it is said] in a song (raga Gauri):
Glory, glory to Ramakrishna Acharya, the steadfast,
the high-minded, giver of happiness, the generous!
Ever absorbed in bhava, greedy for kirtana,
exceedingly skilled in preaching.

125Full of happiness, he delights the minds of rasikas
and dispels the darkness of a mass of sufferings.
Ornament of the brahmana clan, adorned with a host of virtues,
best of panditas, he takes away the pride of the evil-tongued.

126The service of the beautiful Deity of Sri Mohana-raya
is his constant, chief occupation.
Wondrous is his attachment; day and night he rejoices,
drinking the nectar of Gaurachandra's deeds.

127Supremely merciful; the two feet of Narottama
are his all — he knows nothing else.
Who will understand his ways? His lovely fame
Narahari sings and deems himself blessed.

128Sri Thakura Narottama is the purifier of the fallen;
his disciple is Ganganarayana Chakravarti.23

129Ganganarayana is exceedingly learned;
refuting the doctrines of the pashandas, he reveals bhakti.

130Day and night he is intoxicated, drinking the nectar of sankirtana;
poets, floating in happiness, sing of that life.

131Thus [it is said] in a song (raga Gauri):
Glory, glory to Sri Ganganarayana Chakravarti, most steady and profound!
The sweetness of his excellent complexion steals composure; peerless,
most tender and lovely is his body.

132Ever greedy for the rasa of sankirtana,
devoted to graceful dance, lost in prema;
intent on worshipping the lotus feet of Srila Narottama —
the light of the world.

133His mind is immersed in drinking the nectar of Sri Chaitanyachandra's deeds;
he is ever generous.
The charming Deity of Sri Govinda is his life,
his wealth, the support of his very breath.

134Supremely merciful, friend of the lowly,
mighty in power, he takes away the darkness of sufferings.
There is no power to describe his most wondrous fame — renowned,
giving joy to the servant Narahari.

135Thus all the branches and sub-branches of the two,
in their mercy, destroy the misfortunes of living beings.

136What do I know of telling [their] qualities, the supreme elixir?
The fortunate will describe [them] at length.

137Meditating on the feet of Srinivasa Acharya,
Narahari Dasa tells the Bhakti-ratnakara.

Thus in the Sri Bhakti-ratnakara ends the fifteenth wave, called "The Description of the Lives of Sri Shyamananda and Others".

Notes

  1. The Gadadhara in 1 is Gadadhara Pandita; the second Gadadhara here is apparently Gadadhara Dasa.
  2. The original has "শ্রীশঙ্করানন্দময়" (śrī-śaṅkarānandamaya; so also A, scan): taken as "Sri Shankara" + "full of bliss"; a reading as the name "Shankarananda" is also possible.
  3. Sri Acharya is Srinivasa Acharya.
  4. Rayani (রয়নী; today apparently Rohini in Jhargram district, West Bengal) is Rasikananda's native village. The Suvarnarekha is a river flowing through Jharkhand, West Bengal and Orissa to the Bay of Bengal.
  5. By the scan of A: the village is বারায়িত (bārāyita), the river ডোলঙ্গনদী (ḍolaṅga-nadī), "the Dolanga river." The location has not been identified.
  6. Ghantashila (G ঘণ্টাশিলা, A, B ঘণ্টশিলা) is apparently present-day Ghatshila on the Suvarnarekha (Jharkhand), associated with a legend of the Pandavas.
  7. So A (scan: সর্ব্বশ্রেষ্ঠ শ্রীভক্তি) and the 1960 edition (সর্বশ্রেষ্ঠ ভক্তি, sarvaśreṣṭha bhakti); শক্তি in B is an OCR error.
  8. Kishora is Kishoradasa (41), a disciple of Shyamananda; Murari is Rasikananda.
  9. Madhuvana here is the name of one of Shyamananda's disciples.
  10. The reading is confirmed by the scan of A: শ্যামর গৌর, চরিত চয় বিলপত (śyāmara gaura, carita caya bilapata); in the next line, নিরুপম পহু পরি, কর গুণ শুনইতে — পহু পরি কর is taken as pahu-parikara, "the Lord's associates." Śyāmara may also be read as "Shyama [Shyamananda]": "[Shyamananda] laments over the many deeds of Gaura." The translation is conjectural.
  11. Stanza 70 is the last stanza of the song 67–70. Ghanashyama is the poet's signature (bhanita), the second name of Narahari Chakravarti (cf. 90). "Offers himself" renders nichhani, the same as nirmanchhana.
  12. Gopivallabhapura is a village on the Suvarnarekha river (now in Jhargram district, West Bengal), the chief place of Rasikananda's service; Sri Govinda is the Deity he served there.
  13. According to tradition, a Muslim ruler set a wild elephant upon Rasikananda; Rasikananda tamed it and initiated it, and the elephant served the Vaishnavas.
  14. Nā gaṇilā ghara, lit. "he took no account of home": apparently Rasikananda wandered without thought of home; the sense is not quite clear (the reading is confirmed by the scan of A).
  15. Ambikapura is Ambika (Kalna); the Prabhu is Hridaya Chaitanya, Shyamananda's guru (94).
  16. Nitai and Chaitanya are the Deities at Ambika served by Gauridasa Pandita and then by Hridaya Chaitanya (see taranga 8).
  17. Duhkhini Krishnadasa is Shyamananda's former name.
  18. According to tradition, Shyamananda found Sri Radha's anklet (nupura) in one of the groves of Vrindavana; tradition connects this event with his name "Shyamananda" and with the distinctive tilaka of his followers.
  19. Harirama Acharya and Ramakrishna Acharya (121) were brahmana brothers; according to NV, Narottama and Ramachandra Kaviraja converted them, and Harirama became Ramachandra's disciple, Ramakrishna Narottama's.
  20. Krishna-raya is apparently the Deity served by Harirama. By the scans: A অনুপম রসময় অমৃতধার … ভণব কি নরহরি মহিম অপার, the 1960 edition অনুপম বরষত অমৃতধার … ভণব কি নরহরি—মহিমা অপার.
  21. Arya means "noble, worthy." After the 1960 edition: পরমপণ্ডিত ভক্তিপথে মহা আর্য (bhakti-pathe mahā ārya); in A the beginning of the second line is lost in the margin of the scan (ভক্তি-… মহা-আর্য্য).
  22. "Destroys" follows the 1960 edition: নাশয়ে পাষণ্ডমত (nāśaye); in A the beginning of the line is lost in the margin of the scan (…য়ে পাষণ্ড-মত).
  23. Ganganarayana Chakravarti was a learned brahmana, one of Narottama's closest disciples; NV tells of him.
